events.text: The Keeper of the Lotus Ledger is old and tired, and tonight the door of the Knot Room behind the Rolls stands unlatched. On a lacquer tray lies a spool of crimson thread, the kind that is knotted through a heart's meridian and cannot be cut by anyone but its knotter.

effects.log: The thread is warm, like a held hand. You carry it out in your sleeve, and the door is latched behind you.
You latch the door and walk down the White Stairs slowly, hands empty.
The Keeper blinks, thanks you, and records the hour in the Ledger in a hand that does not shake.

events.text: An elder of the House of the Silent Bell dies in the summer, and among the things left to you in the will is a sealed cedar box. Inside is a coil of red thread and a slip of paper: 'Knotted through the heart, it holds one person to one person. Burn this if you are wise.'

effects.log: You put the coil in a drawer with your seals. It is nothing, a drawer-thing, until it is not.

choices.text: Burn it, as the slip says

effects.log: The thread burns with a thin smell of plums, and the smoke goes up in the shape of a knot.

choices.text: Carry it to the Jade Court

effects.log: The Rolls clerk takes the box with both hands and does not look at you for a long moment.

events.text: A pedlar from the Star Sea Pavilion, off a cloud-barge and in no hurry, lays out red threads on a blue cloth. 'Faithful as a tide,' the pedlar says of the last one, and winks, and does not say what it costs.

effects.log: It costs three Mid-grade spirit stones and a promise not to say where you bought it.

choices.text: Tell the pedlar to pack up

effects.log: The pedlar shrugs and rolls the cloth. The thread glints once, and is gone from your mind by evening.

choices.text: Point the pedlar out to a Ministry guard

effects.log: The guard thanks you. The pedlar is gone before the guard has finished the sentence.

events.text: In the rubble of a fallen pavilion on a drifting isle you find a lacquer case stamped with the seal of the Rolls: 'Sealed. Not to be opened by any hand.' Inside, wound on an ivory reel, is a crimson thread that moves a little when you breathe.

effects.log: The reel is lighter than it looks. You tell yourself you are only keeping it safe.

choices.text: Close the case and leave it

effects.log: You set the case back where it was and push a stone over it. The isle drifts on.

choices.text: Take the case to the Court

effects.log: You carry it up the White Stairs. A clerk goes pale, thanks you, and tells you to forget the day.

events.text: {bd7_name}, a disciple of your pavilion, has been offered a seat in the Nine Clouds Palace and means to take it at the next tide of cloud-barges. {bd7_He} has been kind to you for years, and kindness is the only reason this feels like a choice at all.

choices.text: Knot the thread through the heart

effects.log: {bd7_name} sits very still while the thread goes in. The seat in the Palace goes to someone else.
You see {bd7_him} to the barge with a gift of stones. The barge pulls away into white.

events.text: {bd7_name} failed the third trial of the Jade Void Sect today and sits alone in the grotto, hands in {bd7_his} lap. A student who has lost everything will take almost anything. The red thread is in your sleeve.

effects.log: You call it a charm of luck. {bd7_name} lets you knot it through, grateful, and does not see what it is.
You say little. At dawn {bd7_name} stands up straighter than {bd7_he} sat down.

events.text: {bd7_name}, your quickest disciple, can read a cloud-script in a night and will head a house one day. The Star Sea Pavilion has already sent a letter. You could keep that mind beside yours for ten thousand years.

effects.log: The thread goes in while {bd7_he} sleeps. When {bd7_he} wakes, {bd7_he} smiles at you, and the smile is a little too quick.

choices.text: Burn the Pavilion letter yourself, and say so

effects.log: You burn it in front of {bd7_him} and tell {bd7_him} why. {bd7_He} thinks about it, and stays.

events.text: A figure in the grey of the Ministries is caught crouched on a roof-beam of your pavilion, a brush in one hand and your guest-ledger open on {bd7_his} knee. {bd7_name} says nothing at all, which is its own kind of answer.

choices.text: Knot the thread and turn {bd7_him} around

effects.log: The thread goes in. From tonight {bd7_name} writes the Ministries a different ledger, and you read it first.
The Court takes {bd7_him} gravely. Your pavilion is thanked in the Rolls.

choices.text: Strip the ledger of what matters and let {bd7_him} go

effects.log: You black out three pages and let {bd7_him} run. The Ministries get a very dull ledger.

events.text: A courier of the Demon Realm, in plain cloud-cloth, steps off a cloud-barge with a letter sealed in black wax and is stopped by your door-wardens. {bd7_name} is shaking and says the letter is not for you. It is for someone you know.

choices.text: Bind {bd7_him} and read the letter first

effects.log: The thread goes in. {bd7_name} reads the letter aloud to you, voice flat, and you learn what the Demon Realm wanted.

choices.text: Send {bd7_him} to the Court with the letter

effects.log: The Court seals the letter and thanks you. The courier is led away, white to the lips.

choices.text: Burn the letter and send {bd7_him} home

effects.log: You burn it in the lamp. The courier bows low and does not say how grateful, which is wise.

events.text: {bd7_name}, who copies for the Ministries, has been copying your accounts as well, and was caught with the inked brush still wet. {bd7_He} has a child on a drifting isle and is very frightened.

choices.text: Knot the thread through the heart

effects.log: You promise to look after the child. The thread goes in all the same, and {bd7_name} hears the two things and cannot hold them together.
The Court deals with copyists severely. You do not ask how.

choices.text: Pay for the child and send {bd7_him} off

effects.log: You pay a year of stones for the child and see {bd7_him} to the barge, and nothing more is said.

events.text: {bd7_name}, retainer of {bd7_master}, has been sitting in a tea pavilion on the third tier for an hour pretending to read, waiting for you. {bd7_He} has the look of someone who would give a great deal to be out of a bad house.

choices.text: Pour the tea and the thread

effects.log: The tea is jasmine. The thread goes in while {bd7_he} sips. {bd7_He} will tell you every secret of {bd7_master}, and cannot say why.

choices.text: Pay for the tea and listen only

effects.log: You listen. {bd7_name} tells you enough to understand, and not enough to hang a house.

events.text: The barge-pilot of {bd7_master} is a quiet one, who hears every word spoken on deck. {bd7_name} moves between the isles with the doors of a dozen houses at {bd7_his} back. A pilot like that, bound to you, would be the best ear in the Isles.

choices.text: Bind the pilot to your cause

effects.log: The thread slides in while the barge is becalmed. {bd7_name} keeps steering, and for the first time in years keeps nothing back.
You offer a fair price for what {bd7_he} hears. {bd7_name} takes it. The friendship has a limit, which is also an honest thing.

events.text: {bd7_name} wakes smiling and does not know why. The red thread sits in the heart now, glimmering faintly under the skin when {bd7_he} turns toward you. {bd7_He} calls you by the old name, softly, and takes it for friendship.

effects.log: You let it be friendship, since that is the easier word.
You tell {bd7_him}. {bd7_name} says nothing for a long time, and the thread pulls tighter than words.

events.text: {bd7_name} is a better disciple than before, and you know why. {bd7_He} keeps the pavilion's accounts honest, tends the grotto beds, and never once raises {bd7_his} voice. It is a perfect obedience, and you find you do not like to look at it.

effects.log: You order a day of rest. {bd7_name} rests all day, stiffly, as if waiting to be released.
You enjoy it, and by the end of the season you stop noticing you are enjoying it.

events.text: {bd7_name} writes to the Ministries as instructed, in {bd7_his} own neat hand, and the Ministries believe every word. The thread keeps {bd7_him} loyal; it does not keep {bd7_him} from weeping at the lamp afterward.

choices.text: Read the letter, then burn it

effects.log: You read each letter, then burn it. The ash drifts up the window in a dry red curl.

choices.text: Tell {bd7_him} to stop writing for a while

effects.log: You give {bd7_him} a month away. The Ministries notice the silence and grow curious.

events.text: The Ministries' agent bound to you has stopped sleeping well. {bd7_name} brings you the news of the Isles in the grey hour before morning, and the thread glints as {bd7_he} speaks, as if the heart were a lantern held to your hand.

effects.log: You pay well. {bd7_name} takes them without looking, and counts them twice, to have something to do with the hands.
You ask nothing for a week. {bd7_name} does not know what to do with so much quiet.

events.text: {bd7_name} sits across from you at {bd7_master}'s table and cannot say a word against it, and {bd7_master} does not know why the whole house has gone so quiet. The thread is easy to carry. You carry it everywhere.

choices.text: Take what you need and nothing more

effects.log: You take one name, one date, and one key. It is almost modest.
You take every secret of the house, and sleep badly after, as if you had eaten something that was not yours.

events.text: {bd7_name} no longer asks who you are when you come to the door. {bd7_He} opens it, smiles, and steps aside. Somewhere between the second tier and the third, a friendship has turned into a leash, and neither of you has said so.

effects.log: You say it. {bd7_name} says thank you, in the voice of someone who must.
You say nothing. The thread glimmers under the collar, and does its quiet work.

events.text: The thread loosens in the old places, as red thread does, and you could tighten it with a few of your own years: a decade of an immortal's life poured down the knot. It would hold harder, and look less like love.

effects.log: A decade runs from your hands into the knot. The thread glows like a wire, and you feel the tiredness a long time after.
You let it be. The thread slackens a little, and {bd7_name} breathes out for the first time in a month.

events.text: The Knot Room's old texts say the thread drinks blood and gives back faithfulness. You prick a finger over the spool by lamplight and watch the red thread go redder. Somewhere on the isles, {bd7_name} puts a hand to {bd7_his} chest.

effects.log: You give it a second drop. The thread is satisfied. You are a little paler than you were.
You wipe the finger and put the spool away. The thread is half-fed and sulks.

events.text: It is the anniversary of the knotting, and the thread is dull. A century of your life would polish it. A century is nothing to an immortal, and everything to the person it is knotted in.

effects.log: You spend it, and the thread blazes. You feel older by a thing you cannot name.
You spend nothing. Let it be dull. Let it be what it is.

events.text: {bd7_name} brings you a basket of white peaches from the isle's orchard, as every year, and smiles without being asked. The thread glints in {bd7_his} chest as {bd7_he} turns to go. Peaches are the same peaches they always were.

effects.log: You eat one in front of {bd7_him}. {bd7_name} watches you with a strange hunger, as if the eating mattered.

choices.text: Ask {bd7_him} what {bd7_he} would do if free

effects.log: You ask. {bd7_name} says, at length, that {bd7_he} cannot imagine it. You file that away like a splinter.

events.text: At the turn of the year {bd7_name} asks to visit a sister on a far isle. {bd7_He} has never asked leave before. The thread tugs when you hesitate, and you feel it tug in your own hand.

effects.log: You let {bd7_him} go. {bd7_name} comes back on the last day, a little too quickly.
You refuse kindly. {bd7_name} bows and goes to bed early, and the thread dims.

events.text: The Ministries ask {bd7_name} to account for the winter in writing. Every word {bd7_he} sends is true, and every word is chosen by you. The Ministries thank {bd7_him}. Nobody asks how {bd7_he} sleeps.

choices.text: Add a line of your own

effects.log: You add a line, and the Ministries nod over it. It costs the other side a season of good work.

choices.text: Slacken the thread for a day and see what comes back

effects.log: For a day {bd7_name} is only a person at a desk, dazed. {bd7_He} looks at you for a long moment before the thread is drawn tight again.

events.text: {bd7_name}, who spies on the Ministries for you, keeps a lamp in a window on the fourth tier. Every night you see it from your terrace, steady as a pulse. One night in the winter the lamp is dark, and you find that you are afraid.

effects.log: You send a servant. The lamp-oil had run out. You are ashamed of the fear.

choices.text: Light a lamp of your own

effects.log: You light a lamp at your own window, small and steady. In the morning, theirs is lit again.

events.text: {bd7_master} has a new retainer in the hall, and {bd7_name} is slow to bring the old house's secrets any more. It is just the thread settling, but it makes you think how thin the thing is. A heart can be held; it cannot be taught to want to be.

effects.log: You visit, make polite talk, and learn how little {bd7_master} suspects.

choices.text: Release {bd7_name} for a year and see

effects.log: You let the thread go slack. {bd7_name} stays, and you cannot tell whether it is choice or habit.

events.text: {bd7_name} passes you on the White Stairs without a bow. For one moment the eyes are only {bd7_his} own. Then the thread catches, and {bd7_he} turns and bows twice to make up for it.

effects.log: You return the bow, properly, and feel the cost of it more than {bd7_he} does.
You take it. The second bow was never an apology.

events.text: {bd7_name} tried to leave for the Nine Clouds Palace in the night. The thread drew tight at the third landing of the White Stairs, and {bd7_he} sat down where {bd7_he} stood, hands to {bd7_his} chest. In the morning {bd7_he} comes to you grey-faced and kneels.

choices.text: Keep the thread as it is

effects.log: You keep it. {bd7_name} will not try the stairs again for a long while.
You draw the thread back out of the heart, slowly. {bd7_name} weeps once, for no reason {bd7_he} can name.

choices.text: Let the thread finish what it started

effects.log: You do nothing, and the thread does what it was made to do.

events.text: A letter went out in {bd7_name}'s hand to your rivals, and got as far as the gate. The thread drew tight and the letter fell, and {bd7_he} lay in the courtyard until the cranes came to look. Now {bd7_he} waits to hear what you will say.

effects.log: You carry {bd7_him} in. It is the cruelest mercy, and you know it.
You loosen the knot. {bd7_name} stands, uncertain, then walks out through the gate without looking back.
You leave {bd7_him} lying, and the thread does what it was made to do.

events.text: {bd7_name} stands before you, one hand clenched on the thread-knot at the heart, and says in a very level voice that {bd7_he} will not be held like this. The thread burns. {bd7_He} does not fall. {bd7_He} has fought it all night and lost, and wants you to see that.

choices.text: Admire the effort, and keep the thread

effects.log: You admire it aloud, and keep the thread. {bd7_name} looks at you as at a stranger.
You open the knot. {bd7_name} staggers, steadies, and bows. It is the bow of an equal.

choices.text: Hold off the decision a day

effects.log: You ask for a day. {bd7_name} gives it, and the day is longer than a month.

events.text: {bd7_name} moved against you openly, in the Hall of the Rolls before witnesses, and the thread stopped {bd7_him} in the middle of a word. Witnesses saw a person bend double and thought it a fit. You know otherwise.

choices.text: Keep the thread, and call it a fit

effects.log: You send for a physician and the witnesses go home. The thread holds.
You loosen the knot where all can see {bd7_him} straighten. Nobody understands what they saw.
You say nothing, and the thread goes on tightening.

events.text: The thread tore. A rival's counter-spell, a bad winter, or only time: {bd7_name} walked out of the pavilion at dawn and did not look back, and you felt the knot go slack in your own hand like a dropped string. A letter to the Ministries is already on its way.

effects.log: You send men. They return empty-handed and embarrassed.
You let {bd7_him} go. The pavilion feels, for a moment, much emptier and much cleaner.

events.text: {bd7_name} burned the thread out on the sacred fire of a far isle, at the cost of a month of fever and the use of one hand. A messenger comes to tell you. {bd7_He} sent no word for you, only the ash of the thread, wrapped in a white cloth.

effects.log: You keep the ash in a jar on the high shelf. It is a poor sort of trophy.

choices.text: Scatter the ash into the sea of clouds

effects.log: You scatter it off the terrace. The clouds take it in without a sound.

events.text: The knot loosened in the night, and {bd7_name} woke clear-eyed for the first time in years, looked at you, and understood everything. {bd7_He} has already gone, and left the door open, and a single line of writing on the table: a date and a name, as a promise of what is to come.

effects.log: You read it three times. The name is yours.
You burn it. That does not make it less true.

events.text: The thread slipped when you were away on a cloud-barge. {bd7_name} is gone, and the Ministries have been told. By evening a summons arrives at your door with the Jade Court's seal.

choices.text: Answer the summons with a straight face

effects.log: You go. You answer each question the same way, short and plain. It earns you a small bad name and not a large one.
You hide in a high grotto until the summons is forgotten, or at least misfiled.

events.text: The thread failed, and {bd7_name} is gone, and this time they went to the Court with the whole of it: the Knot Room, the spool, your name. Heads turn in the tea pavilion as you walk past, and cheerful people stop speaking.

effects.log: You walk the length of the tier with your back straight. A few people nod. A few do not.
You keep to your grotto for a season. It is not a courageous thing, but it is quiet.

events.text: You draw the red thread out of {bd7_name} on a clear morning, and it comes in one smooth pull, like a hair from a drain. {bd7_He} stands very still for some time. Then {bd7_he} looks at you, as at a stranger, which is what you now are.

effects.log: You say it plainly. {bd7_name} does not answer. The silence has weight.

choices.text: Give {bd7_him} a bag of stones for the road

effects.log: You give the stones. {bd7_name} takes them and goes, and the pavilion is a little less warm.

events.text: The thread is out of {bd7_name} now, and the cranes seem to circle the pavilion more slowly. {bd7_He} stays one more night, politely, to be sure it is real, and in the morning {bd7_he} bows and goes down the White Stairs one step at a time.

effects.log: You watch until the mist takes {bd7_him}. Something in you lets out a long breath.
You call a name. {bd7_name} does not turn. That is its own answer.

events.text: You release {bd7_name} on the anniversary of the knotting, with the Keeper of the Lotus Ledger as witness, and write the release in the Rolls. It costs you nothing but a line in a book. It costs you everything else you were proud of.

choices.text: Sign your own name beneath it

effects.log: You sign. The Rolls will remember it longer than you will.

choices.text: Sign, and say it was nothing

effects.log: You sign, and say it was nothing. Nobody who knows you believes it.

events.text: The Jade Court sends a clerk to the pavilion with a question in a lacquer tube: whether a certain spool was ever drawn from the Knot Room behind the Rolls, and by whom. A Ministry guest watches you read it. The clerk watches your face.

effects.log: You say it was you. The clerk writes it down without surprise, and the Court does not press the matter further than a fine.
You deny it. The clerk bows and goes, but the guest does not look away from your hands for a long time.

choices.text: Name a rival as the thief

effects.log: You point to a rival, with a straight face. The clerk takes the name down, and you take the cost of it with you.

events.text: A cloud-barge brings the news before dawn: the Thread of Binding has been found on a bound person, a retainer of a rival house, and under questioning, the knot-pattern was traced to your hand. The Keeper of the Lotus Ledger asks to see you at noon.

choices.text: Go to the Keeper and confess

effects.log: You go. The Keeper listens, sighs, and writes a short entry. It will be read for a thousand years.

choices.text: Go and say it was not you

effects.log: You go and lie, with a calm face. The Keeper lets it stand, for now.

choices.text: Go and give the Keeper another name

effects.log: You give the Keeper a name. The Keeper writes it with a slow, careful hand.

events.text: Someone left a red thread on your threshold overnight, tied in the old knot. Nobody has to say what it means. By noon the Isles know, and the tea pavilions turn their faces when you pass.

effects.log: You say, loudly, in the tea pavilion, that it is yours. Silence. Then, slowly, talk again.
You deny it with heat. The heat is the giveaway, but the Isles are polite.

choices.text: Say it belongs to a former friend

effects.log: You say a former friend left it. The Isles nod, and some even believe it.

events.text: On an errand of the Jade Court you step down through the cloud-floor to the mortal world for an afternoon, and a bell-founder at a village forge, {dv7_name}, looks up from a hot bell and does not see an immortal. {dv7_He} sees a stranger with soft shoes who is standing in the way of the light.

effects.log: {dv7_name} laughs, and offers you a stool. You sit through a whole casting. Cloud-court errands rarely end this well.

choices.text: Say your errand is none of {dv7_his} business

effects.log: You say it in the voice of the Isles. {dv7_name} bows ironically. The bell, behind {dv7_him}, rings once by itself.

choices.text: Climb back up before anyone sees

effects.log: You climb back up to the Isles. The ring of the bell stays in your ear until evening.

events.text: A crane carries you too low in a storm, and you wake on a rice-terrace with a torn sleeve. A mortal, {dv7_name}, who has been tending the water-gates in the rain all night, finds you and brings a straw cloak without asking who you are. {dv7_He} thinks you are a lost traveller.

choices.text: Accept the cloak and the kindness

effects.log: You accept both. {dv7_name} makes you a cup of ginger water and says nothing about your shoes, which are far too clean.
You thank {dv7_him} the way one thanks a servant. {dv7_name} frowns. You go, with the cloak.

choices.text: Leave a spirit stone on the stool

effects.log: You leave a Low-grade stone on the stool where {dv7_he} will find it. It is a gift too strange to explain.

events.text: From the Isles you have watched a kite-maker's village for forty years, as you watch a garden. Today you come down to see it, and {dv7_name}, the kite-maker's apprentice, hands you a kite and says, "Fly it, then, before the wind drops." {dv7_He} has no idea who you are.

effects.log: It goes up like a bird. You and {dv7_name} stand there laughing, and neither of you notices the cloud-barge pass far above.

choices.text: Say you cannot, it is beneath you

effects.log: You say it with a smile that is not meant to be unkind. {dv7_name} takes the kite back, and the wind drops.
You watch {dv7_him} fly it, and then you are gone, and the kite is a white speck in the sky.

events.text: At the foot of the White Stairs, where the stair meets the mortal ground at a place no Ministry map admits, a lamplighter named {dv7_name} trims the lamps for travellers who come off the cloud-ferries. {dv7_He} lights yours without a word, and asks no fee, and says something you have not heard in a thousand years: "Mind your step."

choices.text: Say thank you, and mean it

effects.log: You say it, and mean it. {dv7_name} nods as if thanks were weather, and trims the next lamp.
You pass by. The lamp stays lit behind you for a long time, steady as a small rebuke.
You ask. {dv7_name} says travellers fall, and a lamp is cheaper than a funeral. You laugh, and then you do not.

events.text: There is a gap in the cloud-floor above the bell-founder's hill where the sky is thin. At the hour of the copper gong you step through it, and {dv7_name} is already waiting with a wrapped dumpling and a bad joke. A year ago you would have called the Isles home without thought.

effects.log: You laugh together until the dumpling is cold, and the gap in the clouds closes like an eyelid.

choices.text: Check the clouds above for watchers

effects.log: You check, twice. {dv7_name} waits patiently, smiling at your caution, and the dumpling is cold anyway.

choices.text: Take {dv7_him} up to the Isles for an hour

effects.log: You take {dv7_him} up through the gap, only to the edge of a garden. {dv7_name} stares at the whole sea of cloud for a very long time.
You say it to the water, not to {dv7_him}. {dv7_name} says nothing, and does not move.

events.text: {dv7_name} is not feeling well this year; the winter was hard on the lowland and the old fever came. You find {dv7_him} on a pallet, grey in the lips, and sit beside {dv7_him} through the afternoon with a pot of mountain tea. Mortals fall ill. You have forgotten how fast.

choices.text: Brew a restoring draught from the Isles

effects.log: You bring a vial of a cloud-herb. The fever breaks in a day. {dv7_name} asks no questions, which is the greatest kindness.

choices.text: Be careful: leave no trace of the Isles

effects.log: You do what mortals do, with a mortal pot and a mortal blanket. It takes longer, and the Ministries never learn.

choices.text: Bring a physician from the Isles

effects.log: You bring a physician in disguise. {dv7_name} recovers fast, and is suspicious for the rest of the year.
You leave. You tell yourself that nursing is not your place. You do not believe it.

events.text: The Ministries have added a watch-tower to the edge of the cloud-floor this year, and the old gap is a hundred paces from it. {dv7_name} has moved the meeting to a boat on the river, among the reeds, where the cranes cannot see. You come to it as a thief comes home.

choices.text: Spend the evening among the reeds

effects.log: You spend the evening among the reeds, listening to the frogs. It is the best evening of your year.

choices.text: Come only at the new moon

effects.log: You come only when there is no moon. It is less often, and safer, and {dv7_name} says it is also lonelier.
You walk down the river road in daylight. The tower does not stir, but a crane lands on the reeds and stays.
You stay on the Isles, among the laughing and the lanterns. The reeds go on without you.

events.text: {dv7_name} brings you a gift each year, small and strange: a cracked cup, a red string, a mud-coloured stone. Today it is a paper boat. "For when the sea of clouds is rough," {dv7_he} says, and doesn't see you laugh until your eyes are wet.

effects.log: You keep the paper boat in a drawer of the Isles, where nobody will find it, and take it out most nights.

choices.text: Wrap it in cloud-silk against the damp

effects.log: You wrap it carefully and hide it in a hollow of the Isles wall. The Ministries will find nothing there.

choices.text: Float it from the highest terrace

effects.log: You float it from the highest terrace in front of everyone. It sails down into the white, a small, defiant thing.
You leave it on the grass. It is a strange place for a gift, but no stranger than where it came from.

events.text: A summer storm cuts the cloud-ferries, and you are stuck below for three nights in the loft of {dv7_name}'s uncle's barn. The rain on the thatch is as loud as drums. {dv7_He} tells you everything about the village, because you ask, and nobody has asked in a long time.

effects.log: You listen to all of it, and by the third night you could draw the village from memory.

choices.text: Slip out before dawn so you are not seen

effects.log: You slip out before dawn. {dv7_name} finds the loft empty and the hay still warm, and understands.

choices.text: Stay a fourth night, storm or no

effects.log: You stay a fourth night. The Isles are two days overdue for you, and someone notices.

choices.text: Go back to the Isles at the first chance

effects.log: You go back at the first chance. The storm in your chest is worse than the one on the thatch.

events.text: At the third meeting of the year a Ministry crane lands at the edge of the field while you and {dv7_name} are sharing a flask. It is an ordinary crane. It is also, you suddenly remember, a very good listener.

effects.log: You hold {dv7_his} hand openly, with the crane watching. After a time the crane flies away.

choices.text: Make small talk about the harvest

effects.log: You talk about the harvest as long as the crane watches. {dv7_name} plays along without a flicker.
You whistle it off, which is not allowed. The crane goes. Somewhere, a page is turned.
You pretend to be strangers, and it is the hardest play you have ever acted in.

events.text: {dv7_name} has started to count the years in a way you do not. "Eighteen springs," {dv7_he} says. "You have not changed." It is said lightly. It is not light. Out on the valley road a funeral procession passes with flutes, and you both pretend not to look.

effects.log: You say it, and know you are promising what you cannot keep forever, only for as long as {dv7_he} has.
You change the subject to the bell-casting. {dv7_name} lets you, carefully.
You tell {dv7_him} all of it, the stairs, the thousand years, the Rolls. {dv7_He} listens without a word, and holds your hand tighter.
You withdraw for the year. The distance is a kind of mercy, you tell yourself.

events.text: On the ridge at dusk, with the cloud-floor lit pink below you and the mortal world spread out to the west, you say what you have not said to anyone on the Isles in a thousand years. {dv7_name} turns to you, and for once has no joke at all.

effects.log: You say it. {dv7_name} says it back, voice shaking. The words go out over the whole valley and nothing answers but a bird.
You say it was a mistake, and the lie costs you something. {dv7_name} nods slowly, as if hearing a verdict.

events.text: {dv7_name} falls ill of an old fever in the third autumn, and on the third night, in the sick-room, hands you a cup of tea and asks, quite gently, whether you have ever been afraid of anything. "Yes," you say. "Of this." That is the confession.

effects.log: You admit it, and {dv7_name} takes your hand and holds it against a hot cheek. The fever breaks in the morning.
You deflect, and leave before dawn. The cup of tea is still warm when you pass the door, in your mind.

events.text: Under the bell-tower of the village, in the hour when the last stroke has faded, {dv7_name} says it first: "I know what you are. I do not care." {dv7_He} has known for years. It was only waiting for you.

effects.log: You tell {dv7_him}. {dv7_name} laughs, once, wetly, and holds on.
You tell {dv7_him} it cannot be. {dv7_name} says, "Then say it and look at me." You cannot.

events.text: A letter comes to the pavilion in the grey of the Celestial Ministries. It is addressed to you, and it contains the name of a village, the name {dv7_name}, and a date of every cloud-gap you went through. It is signed, politely, with a seal you know.

effects.log: You read it to the end. It is thorough, and it is courteous, and there is nothing in it you can dispute.

choices.text: Burn it, and go down at once

effects.log: You burn it and go down to the village that night. The cloud-gap is already watched.

events.text: An old acquaintance from the Star Sea Pavilion mentions over wine, without looking up, that the Ministries have been asking about a certain bell-founder's hill. "A small place," the acquaintance says. "Easily lost." The wine is suddenly sour.

effects.log: You leave early, with a very civil face. The acquaintance watches you go and does not finish the wine.
You ask, and they tell you, and every part of it is worse than you thought.

events.text: It is out. The Keeper of the Lotus Ledger has written it in the Rolls: an immortal of the Isles and a mortal of the red dust, met sixteen times through the cloud-gap. The tea pavilions have been talking about little else for a week.

choices.text: Walk through the talk with your head up

effects.log: You walk through the pavilions, and the talk dies as you pass and rises behind you.

choices.text: Stay away from the tea pavilions

effects.log: You stay in your grotto for a season. The talk grows, as talk does, in the dark.

events.text: The Celestial Ministries summon you to the Hall of Law. The Minister of Rites reads from the Rolls without once looking up: 'Heaven's Law forbids the red dust. Break the tie by the new moon, or be struck from the Rolls.' Behind the Minister, the guards of the Ministries stand in a row.

choices.text: Marry in secret below, and hide it

effects.log: You say you will end it. You go down that night and marry {dv7_name} under a lamp with no witnesses but a cat.

ok.log: You stand in the Hall of Law and refuse. The Ministries, to everyone's surprise, flinch first.

fail.log: You stand in the Hall of Law and refuse. The Ministries do not flinch.

effects.log: You steal a Jade Court ascension slip from the Rolls and carry it down to the village in your sleeve. The ink smells of lotus.
You agree to end it. The Minister nods, and a clerk writes your name in a thin hand.

events.text: The Jade Void Sect sends an envoy, not the Ministries, with a gift of a hundred High-grade stones and a bland smile: end the matter and the stones are yours, and the Rolls forget. A week later the Ministries send an envoy of their own, and he is not smiling.

choices.text: Marry in secret, under a false name

effects.log: You and {dv7_name} are married by the river with the name of a dead acquaintance on the paper. Both envoys are left to guess.

ok.log: You send both envoys away in the same hour. The Isles remember it as the day the Court blinked.

fail.log: You refuse them both. Neither of them is impressed.

choices.text: Carry {dv7_him} up with a forged ascension

effects.log: You forge a seal over a night, and in the morning you walk {dv7_name} up the White Stairs as an immortal of a far isle.

choices.text: Take the stones and end it

effects.log: You take the stones. They are cold, and heavy, and you never spend them.

events.text: The marriage was found. The Ministries come back with the letter from the village registrar, the name on the false paper, and a document with your hand on it. The Minister of Rites reads aloud: 'A second summons. There will not be a third.'

effects.log: You hide it better. The village is moved, quietly, to a far valley, and {dv7_name} goes with it, and the cloud-gap is a new one.

choices.text: Defy the Ministries to their faces

ok.log: You defy them in the Hall of Law again, and this time the Minister bows, a little, with a hard face.

fail.log: You defy them. The Hall of Law has been waiting for this.

effects.log: You spend the last of your standing on a slip of lotus-ink, and go down for {dv7_name}.
You give {dv7_him} up. It is the second time, and it does not get easier.

events.text: A Ministry crane lands on your windowsill with a rolled order: the mortal {dv7_name} is to be struck from the memory of the Isles, and you from the cloud-floor, unless the tie is ended by the turn of the season. The order is signed in three hands.

choices.text: Wed {dv7_him} in secret before the season ends

effects.log: You go down in a plain robe and wed {dv7_him} in the shrine of a village god who does not ask questions.

choices.text: Stand before the three and say no

ok.log: You say no in three different ways to three different signatures. The order is withdrawn with a polite sigh.

fail.log: You say no. The three signatories look at one another, and you realize you have been outvoted.

effects.log: You lift {dv7_name} through the clouds with a ribbon of stolen cloud-silk. {dv7_He} grips your wrist all the way up, laughing.
You let {dv7_him} go. It is the right thing, and it is a terrible thing, and both are true.

events.text: You and {dv7_name} are married at a mortal shrine under a plum tree, with a cat, a ferryman and a very old woman as witnesses, and nobody else. The vow is quick. The tea is hot. For a moment the whole sea of clouds is simply a view from a window.

effects.log: You toast the cat, and the cat does not mind, and {dv7_name} holds your hand and hides a grin in your sleeve.
You burn the paper afterward. The ashes smell of plum-wood, and the secret is safe, for now.

events.text: The Isles give a feast, an actual feast, in your honour: lanterns, cranes, a decorated barge. The Ministries sit in the second row, stony. {dv7_name} walks up the White Stairs on your arm, wearing a robe cut by hand, and no one stops {dv7_him}. It is the strangest sight the Isles have seen in an age.

choices.text: Take {dv7_his} hand on the top step

effects.log: You take {dv7_his} hand on the top step. The cranes lift all at once, and the feast begins.

choices.text: Bow to the Minister of Rites, lightly

effects.log: You bow lightly. The Minister bows back, less lightly, and the pavilion lets out a breath.

events.text: At the top of the White Stairs, a Keeper of the Lotus Ledger writes a new name into the Rolls with a stolen brush, and the line holds. {dv7_name} stands beside you, immortal now, blinking in the high light. The sea of clouds does not know the difference, and neither, quite yet, do you.

effects.log: You show {dv7_him} every grotto, every lantern. {dv7_name} walks as if the floor might fall.

choices.text: Sit down together on the first stair

effects.log: You sit down on the first stair, side by side, and neither of you says a word for an hour.

events.text: The two of you have a small house on the third tier, with a view of nothing but cloud, and a kettle that sings. {dv7_name} still drops tea-leaves on the floor, and you still pretend not to mind. Whatever the Ministries call it, the house is full of ordinary days.

choices.text: Plant a bell-tree in the yard

effects.log: You plant a bell-tree, for the sound. It rings in the evening wind, thin and sweet.
You do nothing at all, together, for a whole afternoon. It may be the best afternoon of the age.

events.text: The Ministries do not kill. They send two clerks in grey, with a bowl of white water and a quiet voice. {dv7_name} is led away down the White Stairs, memory washed, to a village that is not {dv7_his} own, and you are told it is a mercy. No one dies. That is the Ministries' pride.

choices.text: Watch the stairs until they are empty

effects.log: You watch the stairs until they are empty. Nobody tells you to look away.

choices.text: Go down to the new village, anyway

effects.log: You go down. The one who looks up from the well does not know your face. You buy a cup of water and say nothing.

events.text: They struck your name from the Rolls in front of the whole Hall. {dv7_name} is exiled to a far valley, and the cloud-gap above the old village is sealed with three ribbons of grey cloth. You are left with your standing, which is smaller than it was, and your memory, which is not.

effects.log: You take it in silence. There is nothing else to take.

choices.text: Write one letter and burn it

effects.log: You write one letter. You burn it, and the smoke goes down toward the valley, where no one will read it.

events.text: Of all that the Ministries took, the hardest is the small things: the bell-founder's apron on the hook, the paper boat in the drawer, the sound of {dv7_name}'s name. A clerk comes to collect them. You hand over the apron and keep the boat.

effects.log: You keep the paper boat, hidden in a hollow in the wall, where the Ministries do not look.
You give up everything, and the clerk looks almost sorry.

events.text: You end it at the cloud-gap in the first hard frost of the year. {dv7_name} listens without arguing, and thanks you for the years in a voice that is entirely level. You are halfway up the clouds before you find that you are weeping.

effects.log: You do not look back. You cannot be sure whether this is strength.

choices.text: Go back and say one last thing

effects.log: You go back. You say the one last thing. It does not change anything, but it is said.

events.text: It was the Ministries' doing, in the end. {dv7_name} is gone from the village before you can reach it; the house is empty, the forge is cold, and the neighbours say the family left in the night. A white ribbon is knotted on the gate. You do not need it explained.

choices.text: Search the valley roads for a season

effects.log: You search for a season and find nothing. The valley is large, and a mortal life moves quickly.
You let it be. It was never entirely yours to keep.

events.text: You end it on a cold morning, with a flask of warm wine and the village bell sounding the hour. {dv7_name} walks the first half of the road with you in silence and then stops. "Go on," {dv7_he} says. "It is a long way up."

effects.log: You go on. The road is long, and every step of it is clear.
You walk back with {dv7_him} as far as the first house, and say nothing at all.

events.text: In the third year of the secret, {dv7_name} puts a pot of wild plum jam on the table and does not say that it is for you. You eat it from the pot. Somewhere in the Isles the Ministries stay patient, the way a cat stays patient at a hole.

choices.text: Keep a jar for the winter

effects.log: You keep a jar for the winter, in a high cupboard of the Isles, and open it in the dark.

choices.text: Send a jar to the village on the sly

effects.log: You send a jar by a ferryman who asks no questions. The jar comes back empty and washed, which is an answer.

events.text: The Isles have grown used to the mortal in the pavilion. They call {dv7_name} 'the lamplighter', affectionately, because {dv7_he} lights the lamps before anyone asks. Even the Minister of Rites once asked after {dv7_his} health, and flushed to be seen asking.

effects.log: You light the lamps together, from the first terrace to the last, and it takes all evening.
You leave one lamp unlit, out of a small, private mischief, and enjoy the Isles stumbling in the dusk.

events.text: {dv7_name} has to learn how to be immortal the way one learns to walk in a boat. The first decade is balance. The second, patience. You answer every question patiently, and {dv7_he} writes the answers on rice paper and loses them, and you write them out again.

effects.log: You teach {dv7_him} a cloud-script, slowly. {dv7_He} writes it with a bell-founder's heavy hand, and it looks better for it.

choices.text: Ask the Keeper of the Ledger for a year of patience

effects.log: The Keeper gives you a look, and a year of patience, in a lacquer box that you will not open.

events.text: Years later, you hear a small bell at the foot of the White Stairs, and look down. A mortal is carrying a lamp up, stairs and all, and for one moment the walk is so like {dv7_name}'s that your heart stops. It is not. It is a stranger with a lamp.

effects.log: You offer the stranger tea. They sit with you for an hour and ask nothing, and it is the kindest thing of the year.

choices.text: Close the window, and the stranger

effects.log: You close the window. The lamp goes up the stair regardless, and you do not look.

events.text: In the secret years there is a small, dull ache you do not mention: that every spring there is one fewer person in the world who knows how your hand feels in the dark. You keep the spring anyway, the way you keep an old coat.

choices.text: Go down for the spring festival

effects.log: You go down in a plain coat for the spring festival, and stand in the crowd, unrecognised.
You give the festival a miss. The valley carries on, as valleys do.

events.text: The two of you sit on the roof of the house on the third tier and watch the cloud barges move. {dv7_name} says, quite suddenly, "I used to think the sky was empty." "It is," you say. "But it is ours."

choices.text: Stay until the stars come out

effects.log: You stay until the stars come out, and then a while longer.
You fall asleep on the roof with a blanket over you both, and wake with frost in your hair.

events.text: {dv7_name} finds a white hair in the morning mirror and holds it up to the light, like a thread from a weaver. "Look," {dv7_he} says, grinning. "It is the first of my many ranks." You laugh, and your laugh catches in the middle.

effects.log: You pluck it for luck, and keep it in a lacquer box. A small superstition, as good as any.
You say nothing, and kiss {dv7_him} on the forehead. It is the answer.

events.text: The years are in the way {dv7_name} climbs the stairs now: one hand to the rail, a pause on the landing. You slow your own steps to match, and neither of you says why. On the Isles, the cranes outlive three generations of keepers, and no one thinks about it at all.

effects.log: You carry {dv7_him} the last flight, and {dv7_he} grumbles about it, and holds on.
You sit with {dv7_him} on the landing and watch the clouds roll by below.

events.text: At the spring festival you stand in the square with {dv7_name}, and a child asks if the old one is some sort of grandparent to you. {dv7_name} laughs so hard that {dv7_he} has to sit down. You do not laugh. You have never seen the gap so clearly.

effects.log: You take {dv7_him} home early. {dv7_name} falls asleep in the chair with the lantern still lit.

choices.text: Say you are proud to be asked

effects.log: You say you are proud to be asked. The child gives you a candy, which you eat very slowly.

events.text: Every year you bring a gift from the Isles, and every year there are fewer things {dv7_name} can use. This year it is a cushion, soft, from a cloud-weaver. "For my knees," {dv7_he} says, and is too pleased to tease you. You have never been so aware of how much time is gone.

effects.log: You sit on the floor beside {dv7_him}, and {dv7_he} puts a hand on your head as if you were the old one.

choices.text: Say you have a remedy in mind

effects.log: You say you have a remedy in mind, and spend three nights in the Isles looking for it. You find nothing.

events.text: {dv7_name} dies in the spring, in an ordinary bed, with a window open and the sound of bells. You are holding {dv7_his} hand when the breathing changes, and then it is only quiet. Below the window the village goes on casting its bells, and above it the clouds drift without noticing.

effects.log: You stay until the burial, and plant a plum tree on the hill. It is small, and you water it every day for a year.

choices.text: Go back to the Isles at once

effects.log: You go back at once, because you cannot bear the quiet. The Isles are quieter.

events.text: The village bell tolls a long time for {dv7_name}. People come with rice cakes and paper money, and you thank each one, and none of them knows who you are. That night you burn a paper boat on the river. It floats a long way before it sinks.

choices.text: Burn the second boat for the years to come

effects.log: You burn a second boat, for the years you will still have. It is a long sum.
You sit at the cold forge alone, and the bell on its hook rings once, softly, in the draught.

events.text: {dv7_name}'s last words are about the kettle, and whether you remembered to turn off the lamp. They are such ordinary words that for a long time afterward you cannot tell if the sorrow is big or small. In the end you decide it is both.

effects.log: You keep the kettle. It never sings quite right again.
You turn off the lamp. In the dark, the sea of clouds is almost bearable.

events.text: {bt7_name}, whom you have known since the first tier of the Isles, asks a little too lightly about the name you were born under. They ask it over the sixth cup of plum wine, at a stone table among the lanterns. A friend does not ask the same question twice in a week.

effects.log: You say nothing, and from now on you watch. A friend is never watched, and you notice how easy it is.
You tell {bt7_him} the whole of it, hoping it will mend the strangeness. {bt7_name} says only, "Thank you."
You laugh it off. The wine is sweet, and the question hangs.

events.text: A page of your private ledger turns up in the hands of a clerk of the Vermilion Phoenix House, a page you showed to no one but {bt7_name}. The clerk is polite about it and says it was a gift from a friend of yours.

effects.log: You set a watcher. {bt7_name} meets a Phoenix House steward twice in a month.
You ask openly. {bt7_name} says the page was lost, and weeps a little, and you believe it enough to pour tea.

choices.text: Burn the rest of the ledger

effects.log: You burn the rest of the ledger. You will have to write it all again, from memory.

events.text: {bt7_name} has taken to seating you at the end of the long table, next to the door, at the feasts of the Jade Court. They call it modesty. The rival house's envoy, you notice, always sits close to {bt7_name}, and always smiles when you rise.

choices.text: Move to the middle of the table

effects.log: You move, with a smile, and the envoy stops smiling. It is the first thing you have learned all season.

choices.text: Invite {bt7_him} to talk, alone, in a grotto

effects.log: You invite {bt7_him} to a grotto and talk of old days for an hour. {bt7_name} cries, and swears nothing is wrong.

choices.text: Take the end seat and be quiet

effects.log: You take the end seat. The meal is long. The envoy is pleasant to everyone but you.

events.text: At the harvest of the cloud-fruit, {bt7_name} offers you a cup and then, a moment later, takes it back. "It is stale," {bt7_he} says, and pours another. The first cup is poured out on the grass. A drop of it sends the ants into a neat, odd circle.

choices.text: Pretend you did not see, and watch

effects.log: You say nothing. After that you take only the tea you pour yourself.
You say plainly what you saw. {bt7_name} says it was a trick of the light, and the ants go on in their circle.

choices.text: Take the second cup, and pour it on the grass beside the first

effects.log: The ants do nothing at all with the second cup, which was only wine, and you wonder at your own nerve.

events.text: At the {bt7_where}, with the guests of the Celestial Ministries seated in three tiers and the lanterns lit, {bt7_name} rises with a cup in hand, bows to the rival house and, in a clear voice, names your secret. You were watching for it. You are on your feet before the last word.

choices.text: Turn it back on {bt7_him} there and then

ok.log: You name a secret of your own, one that {bt7_name} swore never to repeat, and the guests turn their heads like a field of grass.

fail.log: You open your mouth to answer and the words do not come in time. The silence is {bt7_his}.

effects.log: You endure it in silence, back straight, and let the guests whisper to one another.

events.text: {bt7_name} has chosen the moment well: the fourth course, the harp at rest, the Keeper of the Lotus Ledger half asleep. Your name, your old name, the one from the dust below, is said aloud in a voice of regretful concern, in front of every guest at the {bt7_where}. You saw the weakness in it a month ago.

ok.log: You answer with the date of {bt7_his} own purchase of a seat in the Phoenix House. The harp resumes, in a hurry.

fail.log: You answer, and the answer is not enough. A harp-string snaps, somewhere, with a very small noise.

choices.text: Say nothing and go on eating

effects.log: You go on eating. It is the most difficult meal you have ever had.

events.text: At the {bt7_where}, {bt7_name} bows to the envoy of the House of the Frost Moon and lays a scroll on the table: a page of your private accounts, in your hand. The envoy reads it aloud. You knew this was coming, and still the room goes small.

choices.text: Counter with the envoy's own letters

ok.log: You draw the letters from your sleeve and read the first line. The envoy leaves before the third.

fail.log: You draw the letters, and they are the wrong ones. The envoy smiles faintly.

choices.text: Let the scroll be read to the end

effects.log: You let it be read to the end, with your hands in your lap. It is not a long scroll, as scrolls go.

events.text: You never saw it coming. At the {bt7_where}, with the lanterns lit and the whole Jade Court in attendance, {bt7_name} sets down a cup, smiles at you, and tells the table what you did in your youth. It is true, and nobody had known it but one friend.

choices.text: Bow your head and say it is true

effects.log: You say it is true. It is a small, plain voice, and the table, to its own surprise, quiets.
You stand and leave, with a bow to the host, and the doors close behind you softly.

events.text: Someone has sold your name to the House of the Silent Bell, and the proof is on the table at the {bt7_where} for every guest to pass hand to hand. The hand that wrote it was {bt7_name}'s. You were told, once, that betrayal makes a sound. It does not. It makes a silence.

choices.text: Take the paper and read it calmly

effects.log: You take the paper and read it calmly, to the last line, and pass it on. The room cannot decide what you are.
You leave it unread and finish your tea. A page can only wound someone who lets it.

events.text: The banquet is over. The lanterns are down. Whatever else, {bt7_name} did it, and you were there, and a thousand years of the Isles will remember both. You sit on the terrace at dawn with the cold sea of cloud below, and decide what the rest of the story is.

effects.log: You plan it, patiently, over a decade, as the Isles do everything.
You forgive {bt7_him}, in your own room, with no one watching. It is lighter than you expected.
You cut {bt7_him} out, as one cuts a thread: cleanly, once, without looking.

events.text: A letter arrives from {bt7_name}, three lines long, sealed in the crimson of the House that bought {bt7_him}. It asks for nothing. It says, as if in passing, that {bt7_he} hopes you are well. You hold it over the candle for a long time.

effects.log: You put the letter in a box for later and begin to think.

choices.text: Answer it with a single word: Enough

effects.log: You write the word "Enough" and send it back by crane. It is not the end, but it is a kind of mercy.
You burn it unread. The smoke smells of cheap ink.

events.text: Years pass on the Isles the way tides pass: slowly, and all at once. You see {bt7_name} across a crowded hall of the Jade Court. {bt7_He} sees you, and looks down. Your hands remember how to hold a blade.

choices.text: Cross the hall and ask what you owe each other

effects.log: You cross the hall. {bt7_name} stands, pale, ready for anything but kindness.
You nod once and turn away, and the nod is a door, closing.
You wait. The right season will come.

events.text: Thirty years have passed, and the House that bought {bt7_name} has a weakness in its Rolls. A rumour, a forged entry, a dead man's seal: you can pull the thread and the whole house comes down around {bt7_him}. It will take your whole standing to do it.

ok.log: The house falls. {bt7_name} is left in the rubble with a very small bag.

fail.log: The thread breaks in your hand, and the House turns, slowly, to look at you.

effects.log: You put the rumour back in its drawer. Some debts are better left in the drawer.

events.text: {bt7_name} has risen in the world, high enough to be proud and low enough to be afraid. A Ministry post is open, and your word could place {bt7_him} in it, or sink {bt7_him} for good. A third path is a long quarrel in open court, with the Isles as witness.

ok.log: You fight through three sessions of the court. {bt7_name} is censured in the end, softly and thoroughly.

fail.log: You fight, and lose, and are reproved for bringing a private grudge to a public hall.

effects.log: You say a good word, and the post is {bt7_his}. It costs you something you cannot measure.

events.text: You find {bt7_name} alone on a drifting isle, older, thinner, with a sack of sleeping-rolls and no house left. {bt7_He} looks up. You could finish the old quarrel with a single sentence to the right ear. Or you could sit down.

ok.log: You say the sentence, to the right ear, and by morning there is no isle for {bt7_name} to sit on.

fail.log: You say the sentence, and the right ear has been paid to be wrong. You are the one left standing alone.

choices.text: Sit down on the grass beside {bt7_him}

effects.log: You sit down. You do not say what you came to say. You share a flask.

events.text: The House that bought {bt7_name} has fallen, and so has {bt7_name}'s name. The Isles call it justice. You do not feel that way: you feel like someone who has finished a long, dull errand. The lanterns on the terrace are lit by someone else now.

effects.log: You take the lanterns down yourself, one by one, and fold the paper. It is a small, quiet end.
You leave them hanging. Let someone else have the job of taking them down.

events.text: The Jade Court confirms the verdict at the turn of the year. The Rolls now say that {bt7_name} acted in bad faith, and your name is cleared, and every secret returned. A thousand years from now, a clerk will read the entry and not know either of you.

choices.text: Frame the verdict and hang it by the door

effects.log: You frame it, and hang it by the door. It is the most expensive piece of paper you own.

choices.text: Write the Court a note of thanks

effects.log: You write a short, dry note of thanks. The Court files it without reading.

events.text: You failed. The House kept {bt7_name}, and {bt7_name} kept the Rolls, and you have a wound that is half pride and half something harder. The tea-pavilions have a new story to tell, and in it you are no longer the clever one.

choices.text: Withdraw to a quiet isle for a decade

effects.log: You withdraw to a quiet isle for a decade, and learn to mend a roof.

choices.text: Ask the Keeper for a copy of the verdict

effects.log: You ask for a copy of the verdict and the Keeper, kindly, makes you three.

events.text: The attempt cost you more than you can account for. A Ministry audit has found irregularities in your own books, which your enemies pointed out with great sorrow. You are fined a season of spirit stones and a little of your good name.

effects.log: You pay it quietly. It is the cheapest thing you have learned.
You visit, with a gift, and are received in the cold courtesy that is how the Isles say no.

events.text: You spared {bt7_name}. Nobody noticed, which is how mercy goes on the Isles. Years later, {bt7_name} will lend you a boat in a flood without being asked, and will not say why. The sparing was not done for a boat.

choices.text: Accept the boat, and say nothing

effects.log: You accept the boat, and say nothing, and it carries you well.

choices.text: Send a boat in return, quietly

effects.log: You send a boat in return, quietly, in the next flood. Neither of you mentions it.

events.text: You have forgiven {bt7_name}. The forgiveness came late, but it came whole. On the terrace, a little tea-table is set for two. Neither of you mentions the banquet. A crane lands on the rail and looks at you both with its flat eye.

effects.log: You pour for {bt7_him} first. {bt7_name} holds the cup with both hands, as if it might spill.

choices.text: Take your tea out on the terrace alone

effects.log: You take your tea out on the terrace alone. The cranes watch, unconvinced.

events.text: It is a forgiveness that holds. Years later, the Isles whisper that the two of you have patched it up, and some are glad, and some are sorry for the lost story. You walk down the White Stairs together to a festival on the low ground, and nobody stops to stare.

effects.log: You share a paper lantern. It is lit with your breath and {bt7_his}, and the wind does not put it out.

choices.text: Break a cup together on purpose

effects.log: You break a cup together, on purpose, like children, and laugh until the guards come to look.

events.text: You cut {bt7_name} off, and the cut was clean. There is no letter and no quarrel. Other friends fill the stone table at the banquets, and none of them asks the same question twice. Sometimes you think of the old wine, and the old, careless laughter, and then you think of something else.

effects.log: You take on a new friend, carefully. You are not a fool a second time, only a little more careful.
You keep a seat free at the stone table anyway, in case. Nobody ever takes it.

events.text: A life ago you were betrayed at a banquet in the Isles, and something of it has come down to you: a flinch when a friend asks a question twice, a habit of checking the cup. Your hand tightens on the table. You do not know why.

effects.log: You trust the flinch, and move your seat. It was the right instinct, though you cannot say for what.

choices.text: Let it pass and trust the friend

effects.log: You let it pass. The friend is only a friend, and your heart is a little lighter for it.

events.text: In the quiet before sleep you taste plum wine you have never drunk, and see lanterns you have never lit, and feel a name in your mouth that is not yours. It is all the memory of a friend who sold you, a long time ago.

choices.text: Tell yourself it is a dream

effects.log: You tell yourself it is a dream and sleep, and sleep well.

choices.text: Sit up and write the name down

effects.log: You write the name down. It looks no more familiar on paper.

events.text: In the lower vault of the Book of Fates, where the unwritten pages are kept, a scribe of the Heavenly Court is cleaning a bench and has left a chain of dull silver on it. Each link is a promise, small and sworn, welded shut. Whoever wears it cannot break a word given. The scribe has stepped away.

effects.log: It is lighter than silver and colder than a stone in winter. You slide it into your sleeve, and the vault does not notice.
You leave it on the bench, and go out by the long stair, and the vault goes on keeping its secrets.

choices.text: Call the scribe back and tell the Court

effects.log: The scribe comes back pale, and the chain is in a locked chest by nightfall. The Court notes your name with approval.

events.text: A dying god of the Lineage of the Unlit Lamp calls you to a bedside in a failing temple and presses a single link of silver into your palm. "One word, sworn, and the heart cannot break it," the god whispers. "I used it twice. I would give it back to the vault, if I could stand."

choices.text: Close your hand on the link

effects.log: You close your hand. The dying god sighs, with something like relief, and says nothing else.

choices.text: Give it back to the vault for the god

effects.log: You carry the link to the lower vault and lay it on the bench. The god, in the morning, is easier.

choices.text: Take it to the Heavenly Court

effects.log: You take it to the Court. The Court enters it in a Book, and the god is spared a long inquiry.

events.text: A god of the Silent Drum offers you a link of the Vow-Chain at the edge of a council, with the easy air of someone who has offered before. "I forged it myself," the god says. "The price is a small favour, one day, in a matter of the Drum."

choices.text: Accept the link, and the debt

effects.log: You accept both. The link is a cold little weight in your palm, and the favour sits in your future like a hook.
You decline politely. The god of the Drum smiles with all its teeth, and puts the link away for the next customer.

choices.text: Report the offer to the Court

effects.log: You report it. The Court summons the god of the Drum, who is not smiling now.

events.text: Among the prayers rising from a mortal world one night you find a promise that never reached its god: a vow so fierce that it left the mortal's lips and fell into the vault below as a single loose link. You could pick it up, and use it, and no one would ever know it had been a prayer.

effects.log: You pick it up. It hums faintly with the voice of its sworn mortal, and then goes quiet.

choices.text: Send the link back down as an answer

effects.log: You send it back down. A mortal, far below, finds a promise answered, and does not know why.

choices.text: Hand it to the Court as found goods

effects.log: You hand it in. The Court is a little surprised that you did.

events.text: {bd7_name}, a young god of your temple who keeps the lamps, has been offered a seat in the Lineage of the Hidden Star and means to go before the next feast. {bd7_He} has been loyal to you for a hundred years. That is the reason this feels like a choice at all.

effects.log: {bd7_name} gives a promise at the altar, glad to do it, and the link closes. The seat in the Hidden Star goes to another.
You wish {bd7_him} well and mean it. The temple lamps burn lower that night than usual.

events.text: {bd7_name}, the acolyte you raised from a spark, has just failed an examination of the Heavenly Court, and weeps among the unlit lamps of the lower hall. A god who has lost everything will promise almost anything. The chain is in your sleeve.

choices.text: Ask for one promise, and close the link

effects.log: You ask for a small promise. It closes round the larger one, and {bd7_name} does not see how.

choices.text: Sit with {bd7_him} until the lamps are lit

effects.log: You say little. By the time the lamps are lit, {bd7_name} has stopped weeping, and is humming.

events.text: {bd7_name} is the most gifted of the young gods in your temple and has been noticed by the Laughing River. In a century, {bd7_he} will be a power. In a century, the chain would still hold.

effects.log: The link closes on a vow made over a cup of morning dew. {bd7_name} smiles, and the smile is a little quick.

choices.text: Offer {bd7_him} to the Laughing River yourself

effects.log: You make the introduction yourself. {bd7_name} cries, and goes, and sends you one dew-drop each spring.

events.text: A scribe of a rival pantheon is caught in the margins of the Book of Fates, copying your pages by lamplight. {bd7_name} has the pen still wet. It is not dangerous, only impertinent. It is also a perfect opening.

effects.log: {bd7_name} swears to copy for you, and for no other. The chain closes, and the pen dries.
The Court takes {bd7_him} gravely. Your pages are mentioned in a footnote of the minutes.

choices.text: Let {bd7_him} take the fair copy and go

effects.log: You give {bd7_him} a fair copy, with the dangerous parts left out. {bd7_name} bows, and leaves wondering.

events.text: A messenger of the Nine Wells, who should have no business in your temple, is found at the altar with a notebook, writing the number of your faithful. {bd7_name} blushes to the tips of the ears, and will not meet your eye.

choices.text: Bind {bd7_him} with a link of sworn word

effects.log: You ask for a promise of silence and forge the link round it. {bd7_name} swears, and sends the Wells a gentler report.

choices.text: Send {bd7_him} up to the Court in writing

effects.log: You write the Court a letter. The Wells are reproved, and you are thanked in a hand that does not warm.

choices.text: Burn the notebook and send {bd7_him} home

effects.log: You burn the notebook in the altar-flame. The messenger bows low and says nothing, which is wise.

events.text: A god of the Heavenly Court who is, in fact, a Court informer is found among your temple clerks, with a pocket full of your offerings-ledgers. {bd7_name} stammers that there is a family below who pray to {bd7_him}, and that the Court holds their lamp.

choices.text: Forge a link and turn {bd7_him} around

effects.log: The link closes round a promise to serve you. From tonight the Court reads a different ledger, and you read it first.
You hand {bd7_him} up. The Court deals severely with its own informers who are caught.

choices.text: Pay for the family's lamp and let {bd7_him} go

effects.log: You light the family's lamp from your own flame. {bd7_name} cannot speak for a while.

events.text: {bd7_name}, a lesser god in the household of {bd7_master}, sits in a corner of the Hall of Offerings every evening, listening to the other gods. {bd7_He} listens the way a well does. A god like that, bound to you, would be worth ten spies.

effects.log: The link closes at midnight, over a thin cup of mountain mist. {bd7_name} will tell you every secret of {bd7_master}, and cannot say why.

choices.text: Pay {bd7_him} honestly for what is heard

effects.log: You offer fair offerings for fair words. {bd7_name} takes them with suspicion, and an honest face.

events.text: The cupbearer of {bd7_master} is a god of small things, and sees what the great overlook. {bd7_name} has poured wine for every treaty of the age. A word in {bd7_his} ear is a word in the whole Court.

effects.log: The chain closes round a promise of loyalty at a feast. {bd7_name} pours on, and now every cup is also yours.
You befriend {bd7_him} with ordinary courtesy. It takes longer, and is worth less, and is the only honest way.

events.text: The link closes, and {bd7_name} wakes without knowing why {bd7_he} wants to serve. A silver gleam sits under the skin of the chest when {bd7_he} speaks your name, like a coin at the bottom of a spring. {bd7_He} calls it friendship, because that is the nearest word.

effects.log: You let it be friendship. The chain is quiet, and so are you.
You tell {bd7_him}. {bd7_name} says nothing for a long time, and the silver gleam brightens, as if listening.

events.text: {bd7_name} tends your temple's lamps without being asked, and has never once been late. You have never seen a god so good at serving. It is a perfect obedience, and you are unsettled by how little you had to earn it.

choices.text: Order a day of rest for {bd7_him}

effects.log: You order a day of rest. {bd7_name} rests all day, stiffly, waiting for a word to release {bd7_him}.

choices.text: Accept the service as it comes

effects.log: You accept it, and in a few seasons forget that you ever hesitated.

events.text: The Court receives the weekly reports of {bd7_name}, written in a fair hand, and approves of every one. They are true in every line. You chose which lines. {bd7_name} lights a small lamp at night and sits before it, and the silver gleam under the robe goes in and out like breath.

choices.text: Read the reports before they leave

effects.log: You read each one and put a seal on it. The Court trusts the seal.

choices.text: Give {bd7_him} a week with no reports

effects.log: You give {bd7_him} a week. The Court notices the silence, and asks nothing yet.

events.text: {bd7_name} brings you the whispers of the Heavenly Court at the hour before the first prayer of the day. They are good whispers. They are always good. The chain flickers in the half-light, and {bd7_he} will not look at you while {bd7_he} speaks.

effects.log: You pay generously. {bd7_name} takes it without a word, and counts the grains twice.
You ask for nothing. {bd7_name} does not know what to do with a day like that.

events.text: {bd7_name} sits at the right hand of {bd7_master} at the feast, and when {bd7_master} asks a question, {bd7_name} gives you the answer instead, in a whisper. {bd7_master} wonders why the whole household has gone so quiet. The chain is light to carry. You carry it everywhere.

choices.text: Take one secret and no more

effects.log: You take one name and one date. It is nearly modest.
You take everything, and sleep badly after, as if you had eaten something that was not yours.

events.text: {bd7_name} has stopped asking who you are when you come to the door. {bd7_He} opens it, smiles, and steps aside. Somewhere between the first feast and the second, a friendship became a leash, and neither of you has said so.

effects.log: You say it. {bd7_name} says thank you, in the voice of a god who must.
You say nothing. The silver gleam sits under the collar, and does its quiet work.

events.text: The links of the Vow-Chain grow dull as the years go. A season of the faith that rises to your altar would polish them, the prayers of a whole village poured into the silver. The chain would hold harder, and look less like loyalty.

choices.text: Pour a season of faith into the chain

effects.log: A season of prayers runs from your altar into the links. They shine like new mirrors, and your temple feels very quiet after.
You let them dull. The chain slackens, and {bd7_name} breathes out for the first time in a long while.

events.text: Each link of the chain is a promise, and a new link makes the old ones hold. You could add one: a promise of your own, spoken over the silver, that you will protect {bd7_name} for ever. It would bind you both, and it would be true.

choices.text: Forge a link from your own promise

effects.log: You forge it. The chain glows, and a faint cold runs up your arm, as if the vow were looking at you too.
You keep them unspoken. A chain you do not forge is a chain you cannot be held by.

events.text: On the anniversary of the first link, the chain is dull again. A hundred years of your own life would burnish it, a hundred years from a god who has ten thousand. It is not much to you, and everything to the one it is forged round.

effects.log: You spend them, and the chain blazes. You feel older by something you cannot name.
You spend nothing. Let it be dull. Let it be what it is.

events.text: {bd7_name} sets a small bowl of rice and honey at your altar every year on the day of the first prayer. It is an old custom of the temple, though the custom only started with the chain. The silver gleam under the robe shines when {bd7_he} bows.

effects.log: You eat a spoonful before {bd7_him}. {bd7_name} watches you with a strange hunger.

choices.text: Ask {bd7_him} what {bd7_he} would do if free

effects.log: You ask. {bd7_name} says {bd7_he} cannot imagine it. You file it away like a splinter.

events.text: {bd7_name} asks, for the first time in a century, to visit a sister who keeps a well in a distant world. The chain tugs when you hesitate, and you feel it tug in your own hand.

effects.log: You let {bd7_him} go. {bd7_name} comes back on the last day, a little too quickly.
You refuse kindly. {bd7_name} bows and goes to the lamps, and the silver dims.

events.text: The Heavenly Court asks {bd7_name} to account for the year in writing. Every word {bd7_he} sends is true, and every word is chosen by you. The Court thanks {bd7_him}. Nobody asks how a god sleeps.

choices.text: Add a line of your own

effects.log: You add a line, and the Court approves it. It costs a rival temple a season of good work.

choices.text: Slacken the chain for a day and see what comes back

effects.log: For a day {bd7_name} is only a god at a desk, dazed. {bd7_He} looks at you for a long moment before the chain is drawn tight again.

events.text: {bd7_name}, who keeps an ear in the Court for you, lights a lamp at the western gate of the Court each night. You see it from your own gate, small and steady as a pulse. One winter the lamp is dark, and you find that you are afraid.

choices.text: Send a lesser god to look

effects.log: You send one. The oil had run out. You are ashamed of the fear.

choices.text: Light a lamp at your own gate

effects.log: You light a lamp at your own gate, small and steady. In the morning, theirs is lit again.

events.text: {bd7_master} has a new cupbearer, and {bd7_name} is slow to bring the household's secrets any more. It is only the chain settling, but it makes you think how thin the thing is. A word can be sworn; it cannot be taught to be meant.

effects.log: You visit, make polite talk, and learn how little {bd7_master} suspects.

choices.text: Release {bd7_name} for a year and see

effects.log: You let the chain hang slack. {bd7_name} stays, and you cannot tell whether it is choice or habit.

events.text: {bd7_name} passes you in the Hall of Offerings without a bow. For one breath the eyes are only {bd7_his} own. Then the chain catches, and {bd7_he} turns back and bows twice to make up for it.

effects.log: You return the bow, properly, and feel the cost of it more than {bd7_he} does.
You take it. The second bow was never an apology.

events.text: {bd7_name} tried to leave for the Lineage of the Hidden Star in the dead hour. The chain drew tight at the third gate, and {bd7_he} sat down in the road with both hands to {bd7_his} chest. In the morning {bd7_he} comes to you grey-faced and kneels.

choices.text: Keep the chain as it is

effects.log: You keep it. {bd7_name} will not try the gates again for a long while.

choices.text: Strike the link from the chain

effects.log: You draw the link back and break it on the altar. {bd7_name} weeps once, for no reason {bd7_he} can name.

choices.text: Let the chain finish what it started

effects.log: You do nothing, and the chain does what it was made to do.

events.text: A prayer went up from {bd7_name} to a rival god, and got as far as the clouds. The chain drew tight and the prayer fell, and {bd7_he} lay on the temple floor until the lamps guttered. Now {bd7_he} waits to hear what you will say.

effects.log: You lift {bd7_him} and carry {bd7_him} in. It is the cruelest mercy, and you know it.
You loosen the chain. {bd7_name} stands, uncertain, then walks out through the gate without looking back.
You leave {bd7_him} lying, and the chain does what it was made to do.

events.text: {bd7_name} stands before you, one hand clenched on the chain beneath the robe, and says in a very level voice that {bd7_he} will not be held like this. The silver burns. {bd7_He} does not fall. {bd7_He} has fought it all night and lost, and wants you to see that.

choices.text: Admire the effort, and keep the chain

effects.log: You admire it aloud, and keep the chain. {bd7_name} looks at you as at a stranger.
You open the last link. {bd7_name} staggers, steadies, and bows. It is the bow of an equal.

choices.text: Ask for a day to decide

effects.log: You ask for a day. {bd7_name} gives it, and the day is longer than a century.

events.text: {bd7_name} moved against you in open council at the Court of the Twelve, and the chain stopped {bd7_him} in the middle of a word. The council saw a god bend double and thought it a fit. You know otherwise.

choices.text: Keep the chain, and call it a fit

effects.log: You call for a healer, and the council goes home. The chain holds.
You loosen the chain where all can see {bd7_him} straighten. Nobody understands what they saw.
You say nothing, and the chain goes on tightening.

events.text: A link split. The workmanship of the vault was poor, or a rival's prayer found the crack, or only time did it: {bd7_name} walked out of your temple at dawn and did not look back, and you felt the chain go slack in your hand like a dropped rope. A letter to the Court is already on its way.

effects.log: You send gods. They return empty-handed and embarrassed.
You let {bd7_him} go. The temple feels, for a moment, much emptier and much cleaner.

events.text: {bd7_name} melted the chain in the sacred fire of a far hearth, at the cost of a long fever and the use of a hand. A messenger comes to tell you. {bd7_He} sent no word, only the ash of the silver, wrapped in a white cloth.
