events.text: You end it at the water's edge in the first frost of the year. {dv7_name} listens without arguing, and thanks you for the years in a voice that is entirely level. You are halfway up the lane before you find that you are weeping.

effects.log: You do not look back. You cannot be sure whether this is strength.

choices.text: Go back and say one last thing

effects.log: You go back. You say the one last thing. It does not change anything, but it is said.

events.text: It was the Rolls' doing, in the end. {dv7_name} is moved before you can reach the shrine; the bank is bare, the cup is gone, and the old fisherman says the god was called away in the night. A white ribbon is tied on the gate. You do not need it explained.

choices.text: Search the river for a season

effects.log: You search for a season and find nothing. The river is long, and a mortal life is short.
You let it be. It was never entirely yours to keep.

events.text: In the third year of the secret, {dv7_name} leaves a pot of wild-plum jam on the shrine step and does not say it is for you. You eat it with a wooden spoon, in the rain. Somewhere above, the Keeper stays patient, the way a heron stays patient at a pond.

choices.text: Keep a jar for the winter

effects.log: You keep a jar for the winter, in a high cupboard, and open it in the dark.

choices.text: Leave a reed flute on the step

effects.log: You leave a reed flute. It is the smallest sign a mortal can give, and it is read at once.

events.text: The village has grown used to the pair of you. They call {dv7_name} 'the lamp-boatman', affectionately, because {dv7_he} lights the boats before anyone asks. Even the Keeper of the Rolls once asked after {dv7_his} health, and flushed to be seen asking.

effects.log: You light the boats together, from the first jetty to the last, and it takes all evening.

choices.text: Invite the Keeper to the lighting

effects.log: You invite the Keeper to the lighting, and the Keeper comes. It is a small victory, and you take it.

events.text: {dv7_name} has to learn how to be a mortal the way one learns to walk in a boat. The first year is balance. The second, patience. You answer every question patiently, and {dv7_he} writes the answers on rice-paper and loses them, and you write them out again.

effects.log: You teach {dv7_him} slowly. {dv7_He} fishes with a god's patience and a beginner's luck, and catches nothing at all.
You take {dv7_him} to market. {dv7_He} haggles for a cabbage as if it were a treaty.

events.text: Years later, a small bell sounds at the shrine gate, and a stranger comes up the path with a lantern. For one moment the walk is so like {dv7_name}'s that your heart stops. It is not. It is a pilgrim with a lantern.

effects.log: You offer the pilgrim tea. They sit with you for an hour and ask nothing, and it is the kindest thing of the year.

choices.text: Close the gate on the pilgrim

effects.log: You close the gate. The lantern goes up the path regardless, and you do not look.

events.text: You find a white hair in the washing-bowl and hold it up to the lamp, and {dv7_name}, who has not changed since the day you met, takes it from you with a grave face. "The first of your many ranks," {dv7_he} says. You laugh, and your laugh catches in the middle.

choices.text: Tuck it in the shrine for luck

effects.log: You tuck it into the shrine, with the pebbles. A small superstition, as good as any.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let {dv7_him} kiss your forehead

effects.log: You say nothing, and let {dv7_him}. It is the answer.

events.text: The years show in the way you climb the bank now: a hand to the willow, a pause on the slope. {dv7_name} slows to match, and neither of you says why. Gods outlive a thousand fishermen, and no one in the village thinks about it at all.

choices.text: Let {dv7_him} carry you the last bit

effects.log: You let {dv7_him} carry you the last bit, and grumble about it, and hold on.

choices.text: Sit on the slope and rest

effects.log: You sit on the slope and rest, and listen to the water talk.

events.text: At the harvest fair a child asks {dv7_name} if you are {dv7_his} grandparent. {dv7_name} laughs so hard that {dv7_he} has to sit down. You do not laugh. You have never seen the gap so clearly.

effects.log: You go home early. {dv7_name} falls asleep in the chair with the lamp still lit.

choices.text: Say you are proud to be asked

effects.log: You say you are proud to be asked. The child gives you a honey-cake, which you eat very slowly.

events.text: Your last year comes quietly, in the same bed you were born in, with the shutters open and the sound of the river. {dv7_name} sits at your side, as {dv7_he} has for decades, shining faintly in the lamplight. You say a few things; {dv7_he} says a few things. They are plain and they are enough.

effects.log: You hold {dv7_his} hand, which is cool as a stream and does not tremble. It is the best last year of any.

choices.text: Ask {dv7_him} to sing the old song

effects.log: You ask for the old song of the first ferry. {dv7_name} sings it, thin and sweet, and the river joins in.

events.text: In your last year you ask {dv7_name} to take you to the water once more, and {dv7_he} carries you in a basket to the shallows, as you once carried {dv7_him} a jug. The river holds you up. You float, and the sky is a bowl, and nobody is in any hurry.

choices.text: Float until the stars come out

effects.log: You float until the stars come out, and then a while longer.
You say it, plainly, to the water. {dv7_name} says it back, and the river keeps both.
